```plato
    // The variance of a uniform variable: (Max - Min)^2 / 12.
    Variance(self: UniformDistribution): Number
        => (self.Max - self.Min).Square / 12.0;
```

```plato
    //==
    // # NormalDistribution
    //
    // Parameterization: (mean, STANDARD DEVIATION) — the second field is sigma,
    // NOT sigma squared. Precondition: StandardDeviation > 0. `Mean` is already
    // discharged by the field of the same name.
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Normal_distribution

    // The variance: the square of the standard deviation.
    Variance(self: NormalDistribution): Number
        => self.StandardDeviation.Square;
```

```plato
    // The variance of the variable itself:
    // (exp(sigma^2) - 1) * exp(2*mu + sigma^2).
    Variance(self: LogNormalDistribution): Number
        => (self.LogStandardDeviation.Square.Exp - 1.0)
         * (2.0 * self.LogMean + self.LogStandardDeviation.Square).Exp;
```

```plato
    // The variance: nu / (nu - 2). Precondition: DegreesOfFreedom > 2; the
    // variance is infinite on (1, 2] and undefined at or below 1.
    Variance(self: StudentTDistribution): Number
        => self.DegreesOfFreedom / (self.DegreesOfFreedom - 2.0);
```

```plato
    // The variance is undefined. By the convention stated on the type, this
    // reports positive infinity, spelled as 1.0/0.0 — which is exactly the IEEE
    // +Infinity on every float backend, so it needs no constant. Deliberately
    // NOT adding a `PositiveInfinity` to `INumericalLimits`: that interface is
    // declared in the core/algebra interface files (owned elsewhere) and a new
    // member imposes a fresh obligation on every INumerical implementor
    // tree-wide, which is out of proportion to this one call.
    Variance(self: CauchyDistribution): Number
        => 1.0 / 0.0;
```

```plato
    Variance(self: WeibullDistribution): Number
        => self.Scale.Square
         * (Gamma(1.0 + 2.0 / self.Shape) - Gamma(1.0 + 1.0 / self.Shape).Square);
```

```plato
    // The variance: x_m^2 * alpha / ((alpha-1)^2 * (alpha-2)). Precondition:
    // Shape > 2 — the variance is infinite for Shape <= 2.
    Variance(self: ParetoDistribution): Number
        => self.MinimumValue.Square * self.Shape
         / ((self.Shape - 1.0).Square * (self.Shape - 2.0));
```

```plato

    // The variance: (a^2 + b^2 + c^2 - ab - ac - bc) / 18.
    Variance(self: TriangularDistribution): Number
        => (self.Min.Square + self.Max.Square + self.Mode.Square
            - self.Min * self.Max - self.Min * self.Mode - self.Max * self.Mode)
         / 18.0;
```

```plato
    // The circular variance 1 - I1(kappa)/I0(kappa): 0 as kappa -> infinity
    // (all mass at the mean direction), 1 at kappa = 0 (uniform on the circle,
    // since I1(0) = 0 and I0(0) = 1).
    Variance(self: VonMisesDistribution): Number
        => 1.0 - BesselI1(self.Concentration) / BesselI0(self.Concentration);
```

```plato
    // The variance of the outcome index, as E[i^2] - E[i]^2.
    Variance(self: DiscreteDistribution): Number
        => self.Weights.Count.Range
            .Map(i => i.ToNumber.Square * self.Weights[i])
            .Reduce(0.0, (total, term) => total + term)
         / self.TotalWeight
         - self.Mean.Square;
```
